season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is working back from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season and Kansas City's 10.5 win total prices a full rebound, but his exact camp ramp is still being managed (verify) — in a 6-pt passing TD league he only returns to the top tier if the knee lets him climb the pocket and scramble.

Minnesota named Kyler Murray the Week 1 starter over J.J. McCarthy after Murray dominated first-team reps, and a rushing QB with 6-pt passing TDs and rush yards at 10 yds/pt is exactly the ceiling profile this league pays for while McCarthy craters to waiver fodder.

The Rams are Super Bowl favorites at +550 with an 11.5 win total after acquiring Myles Garrett, meaning positive game scripts and a high team total that lift every LA skill player; Puka Nacua's groin soreness is minor but worth monitoring through camp.

Mike McDaniel is now calling the Chargers offense, importing wide-zone runs, heavy motion and manufactured touches — Omarion Hampton inherits a scheme that historically feeds RB yardage, the stat this league actually pays, while Ladd McConkey gets YAC volume.

The coaching carousel rewired half the league: Brian Daboll (TEN), Kevin Stefanski (ATL), Mike McCarthy (PIT), Klint Kubiak (LV) and John Harbaugh (NYG) took over teams, with Matt Nagy (NYG) and Zac Robinson (TB) as new play-callers — every one of those offenses has repriced fantasy roles this month.

Las Vegas is sitting No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza behind Kirk Cousins to open the year, capping the Raiders' pass-game ceiling and making their receivers (Bech, Tucker, Nailor) snap-count reads rather than locked-in targets.

Preseason injuries are reshaping RB rooms right now: No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love (ARI) suffered a high-ankle sprain with a 3-5 week timeline, Zach Charbonnet (SEA) is on PUP boosting George Holani, Josh Jacobs (GB) is out about a week with a groin, and Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s foot injury hands Bhayshul Tuten the Jacksonville lead.

Return-yardage scoring is a hidden edge this draft season: Chimere Dike led the NFL with 1,986 return yards (roughly +3 ppg at 20 yds/pt), and KaVontae Turpin, Marvin Mims, Ray Davis and rookie Zachariah Branch all carry locked-in or likely return roles worth an extra 2.5-3.4 ppg.

Malik Nabers has returned to practice from his torn ACL and is tracking toward Week 1 in Matt Nagy's West Coast scheme, where analysts see top-five upside if the knee holds — a discounted TD-and-yardage ceiling play (verify his final Week 1 status).

Suspensions are already landing: Falcons pass rusher James Pearce Jr. is banned 8 games from Aug 30, softening Atlanta's pass rush for opposing QBs through October, with Nazeeh Johnson (TEN, 6 games) and Phidarian Mathis (BUF, 3 games) also out — streaming QBs and DSTs against those units early is live.

teams.outlook: A league-low 3.5 win total with Jacoby Brissett bridging to rookie Carson Beck and No. 3 pick Jeremiyah Love (high-ankle sprain, 3-5 weeks) opening behind Tyler Allgeier — a low team total that caps every Cardinal, with Allgeier the short-term TD beneficiary.

Kevin Stefanski takes over with Tua Tagovailoa starting while Michael Penix Jr. rehabs his ACL and pass rusher James Pearce Jr. suspended 8 games; a 6.5 win total means modest team totals, but rookie Zachariah Branch's dual return role is real weekly points in this format.

New play-caller Declan Doyle brings a motion-heavy quick game with downfield shots, setting up Lamar Jackson as the premium bounce-back at 6-pt passing TDs plus rush yardage, with Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews the usage winners behind an 11.5 win total.

Buffalo has beaten its win total six straight years and sits at 10.5, and Ray Davis pairs backfield touches with a league-best 30.4 yards per kick return — sneaky standalone value at 20 return yds/pt.

The reigning NFC South champs (7.5 wins) have a healthier defense, but the backfield is murky: Chuba Hubbard is week-to-week with a hamstring while Jonathon Brooks' recovery looms, so neither back is a stable early-round pick.

Ben Johnson's Bears won 11 games but drew the league's toughest schedule (win total cut to 9.5), Luther Burden III (groin) is missing the preseason, and the Kyle Monangai/D'Andre Swift split plus a 3-way left tackle mess make the run game hard to trust.

A 10.5 win total on the third-easiest schedule keeps the pass offense in shootout mode, but the pass rush replaced Trey Hendrickson with Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy — expect high team totals both ways, and Charlie Jones' kick-return volume is a DST-week streamer angle.

The QB job between Deshaun Watson (multi-INT practices) and Shedeur Sanders is unsettled, but rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are starting over Jerry Jeudy — the young WRs are the only Browns with upside at a 5.5 win total.

Dallas (9.5 wins) added defensive pieces in Rashan Gary and Caleb Downs, Javonte Williams is a TD-regression risk after 11 scores on a snap-dependent role, and KaVontae Turpin's 1,814 kick-return yards make him a legitimate flex in this scoring.

Vegas cut Denver to 9.5 wins after a 14-win season built on close games, but Marvin Mims is now a starting WR on top of leading the NFL in punt-return yards — a deep-threat-plus-returner profile built for this league; Jaylen Waddle (leg strain) should be back next week.

A 10.5 win total on the sixth-easiest schedule keeps Detroit's offense drafting-relevant, and Isiah Pacheco (sprained MCL, expected Week 1) brings a physical TD-hunting style to the backfield — his health status is the thing to watch (verify).

Green Bay's pecking order is shifting: rookie-contract WR Matthew Golden is running two-WR sets ahead of Jayden Reed, Josh Jacobs is out about a week with a groin (MarShawn Lloyd the clear No. 2), and Tucker Kraft is back in team drills off his ACL targeting Week 1.

Houston (9.5 wins after a 12-win year) has Tank Dell nursing a knee and lost backup Graham Mertz to a likely torn ACL, while Jaylin Noel's dual return role plus a bigger year-two offensive role gives him quiet weekly value at 20 return yds/pt.

Daniel Jones enters as the starter with an injury question hanging over him (verify) and Riley Leonard OR Anthony Richardson listed at backup — a 7.5 win total and QB instability keep Colts pass-catchers volatile.

After a 13-win turnaround the total sits at just 8.5 due to free-agent losses, but Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s foot injury breaks the RB co-starter tie toward Bhayshul Tuten, and Parker Washington's league-leading two punt-return TDs add real points in this format.

Everything keys on Mahomes' ACL return (10.5 win total prices a rebound): if he's fully mobile the 6-pt passing TD scoring makes him elite again, but L'Jarius Sneed is managing a knee and the offense's camp reps are being handled cautiously (verify).

New coach Klint Kubiak is starting Kirk Cousins over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza, muting the ceiling; Jack Bech is the listed starter but Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker out-snapped him with Cousins, so no Raiders WR is trustworthy yet.

Mike McDaniel's wide-zone, motion-heavy scheme arrives from the OC chair — Omarion Hampton is the headline non-PPR winner with Keaton Mitchell the handcuff, and Ladd McConkey becomes a YAC-yardage magnet even without PPR juice.

Super Bowl favorites (+550, league-high 11.5 wins) after trading for Myles Garrett — a strong team total floats every Rams skill player, and Puka Nacua's groin soreness is considered minor but worth tracking through August.

A 4.5 win total (second-lowest) and a $67.5M bet on Malik Willis signal a transition year; rookie Caleb Douglas has been Willis' most consistent target and Malik Washington stacks slot work with heavy kick-return volume — the only Dolphins angles worth drafting.

Kyler Murray was named the Week 1 starter, giving Justin Jefferson a more aggressive downfield QB and making Murray a 6-pt-TD-league QB1 candidate, while Aaron Jones OR Jordan Mason remains a true committee to avoid paying up for.
The Super Bowl runner-up's total was trimmed to 10.5 on a tougher schedule; the offense returns largely intact, with the Jam Miller vs. Lan Larison RB3 battle only mattering for handcuff drafters.

Kellen Moore hands Tyler Shough the full-time job with an easy schedule (7.5 wins), but rookie WR Jordyn Tyson's repeat hamstring injury may extend into Week 1 — his August draft cost currently outruns his September role.

The John Harbaugh era with Matt Nagy calling a West Coast, back-friendly scheme repositions the offense: Malik Nabers is tracking toward Week 1 off his ACL with top-five upside if healthy (verify), Cam Skattebo profiles for goal-line work, and the Likely/Johnson/Manhertz TE rotation is a fantasy dead zone.

Geno Smith (last in passing yards per game in 2025) is under real pressure from rookie Cade Klubnik, who started with the first team against Tampa; a 5.5 win total and TE Kenyon Sadiq's groin setback leave little here beyond DST-streaming against them.

New play-caller Sean Mannion adds wide-zone and more RB passing-game work — Saquon Barkley's expanded receiving role adds yardage (not catches, which is fine here), and DeVonta Smith (day-to-day hamstring) has an uncontested target share at a 10.5 win total.

Mike McCarthy inherits a 8.5-win reset with rookie Drew Allar impressing in his debut (80.5 PFF grade), and Jaylen Warren holding the starting RB job over free-agent addition Rico Dowdle — Warren is the Steelers back to draft.

San Francisco (9.5 wins) is already banged up — George Kittle on PUP with an Achilles, Ricky Pearsall out for the year post-PCL surgery, Christian Kirk nursing a calf — which funnels targets to a returning Deebo Samuel (also the listed top kick returner, a bonus in this scoring) and makes camp star De'Zhaun Stribling a live late flyer.

The defending champs sit at 10.5 after losing defensive pieces, and with Zach Charbonnet on PUP, George Holani is the listed starter over first-rounder Jadarian Price — Holani is a cheap early-season TD play, and Rashid Shaheed's dual return role fits this league perfectly.

Zac Robinson installs a McVay-tree offense that features Emeka Egbuka (toe, optimistic for Week 1) as the lead receiver, while Baker Mayfield plays out a contract year feeling disrespected — a motivated QB at 8.5 wins keeps the pass game draftable.

Brian Daboll's RPO and play-action-vertical scheme is built around Cam Ward's year-two leap (6.5 wins, even money), but the backfield is fracturing — Tony Pollard played fewer starter snaps than Tyjae Spears — and Chimere Dike's league-leading 1,986 return yards make him a top return-league asset.

The total dropped to 7.5 partly on Jayden Daniels' health question (verify), Marcus Mariota (MCL) is out for the preseason thinning the QB room, and rookie Kaytron Allen's 23-carry, 85-yard preseason signal points to the early-down, goal-line role this league rewards.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's wide-zone Chargers scheme historically inflates RB rushing yardage and TDs — the two currencies of this non-PPR format — and Hampton has the backfield essentially to himself with only Keaton Mitchell behind him.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Skattebo
breakout_watch.why: Matt Nagy's Giants scheme projects him for goal-line and short-area work; goal-line carries are the single most valuable role in a non-PPR league with TD-driven scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Was already a listed co-starter in Jacksonville, and Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s foot injury clears the path to lead early-down and goal-line work in an offense coming off 13 wins.

breakout_watch.name: Kaytron Allen
breakout_watch.why: Washington gave him 23 carries (85 yards, TD) in the preseason opener — an unmistakable early-down workload signal, and volume rushers convert directly to points at 10 rush yds/pt.

breakout_watch.name: George Holani
breakout_watch.why: Listed starter for the defending-champ Seahawks with Zach Charbonnet on PUP and first-rounder Jadarian Price buried — a free square for early-season TDs on a team with a 10.5 win total.

breakout_watch.name: Tyjae Spears
breakout_watch.why: Out-snapped Tony Pollard with the Titans starters (12 to 9) in the preseason opener; if the flip completes he gets Brian Daboll's top-10-rushing-emphasis workload at a bench-round price.

breakout_watch.name: Jaylen Warren
breakout_watch.why: Holding the Steelers starting job over Rico Dowdle on Mike McCarthy's run-leaning offense — lead-back carries at a committee price.

breakout_watch.name: Matthew Golden
breakout_watch.why: Running two-receiver sets ahead of Jayden Reed in Green Bay; a downfield yardage-and-TD profile beats Reed's slot catch-volume profile in a league that pays zero for receptions.

breakout_watch.name: Zay Flowers
breakout_watch.why: Declan Doyle's motion-heavy Ravens scheme projects a usage spike, and Flowers' YAC/deep-ball profile converts to yardage points with a healthy Lamar Jackson lifting the whole offense.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Zac Robinson's McVay-tree offense features him as the lead Tampa receiver (toe injury minor, optimistic for Week 1) — lead-role yardage and end-zone targets in a healthy passing offense.

breakout_watch.name: Chimere Dike
breakout_watch.why: Led the NFL with 1,986 return yards — at 20 return yds/pt plus 6-pt return TDs that is roughly a 3 ppg head start before he runs a single route in Daboll's offense.

breakout_watch.name: Marvin Mims
breakout_watch.why: Now a listed starting Broncos WR while also leading the league in punt-return yardage — the deep-threat-plus-returner double dip is the exact archetype this scoring system overpays relative to market.

breakout_watch.name: Zachariah Branch
breakout_watch.why: Poised to win both Falcons return jobs as a rookie with elite speed; locked dual return duty alone is worth 2.5-3.4 ppg here, with WR4 receiving upside stacked on top.

breakout_watch.name: KC Concepcion
breakout_watch.why: Running with Cleveland's first team as a rookie and already producing (3 catches plus a 14-yard TD run) — gadget/rushing usage adds non-PPR yardage other rookie WRs don't get.

fade_watch.name: Javonte Williams
fade_watch.why: His 11-TD 2025 is a classic regression setup built on a top-10 snap share that may not repeat — a top-35 ADP prices in the TDs staying, and in a TD-driven format that regression hits hardest.

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: Week-to-week with a hamstring while Jonathon Brooks trends healthier; even a partial Brooks return splits the Carolina backfield and strands Hubbard's round-6 price.

fade_watch.name: Tony Pollard
fade_watch.why: Played fewer first-team snaps than Tyjae Spears in the preseason opener with Nicholas Singleton also in the mix — a fading grip on volume in a scoring system that is all about volume yardage and TDs.

fade_watch.name: Jayden Reed
fade_watch.why: Matthew Golden is running ahead of him in two-WR sets, and Reed's slot catch-volume profile is exactly what a zero-PPR league refuses to pay for.

fade_watch.name: Rachaad White
fade_watch.why: A pass-catching specialist on roughly 30 snaps a game in run-heavy Washington — receptions are worth zero here, which guts the one thing his profile offers.

fade_watch.name: Jerry Jeudy
fade_watch.why: Rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are starting ahead of him in Cleveland's three-wide sets while the QB room (Watson vs. Sanders) is a mess — a name-brand price on a tenuous role.

fade_watch.name: Isaiah Likely
fade_watch.why: Played only 6 of 14 first-team snaps in a three-way Giants TE rotation — TE11 pricing for a timeshare with no locked red-zone role.

fade_watch.name: Carnell Tate
fade_watch.why: A round-5/6 ADP in a crowded Titans target tree where Wan'Dale Robinson likely leads in targets and Cam Ward is still erratic (5-of-12 in the preseason opener) — the cost assumes a leap the situation doesn't support.

fade_watch.name: Kyle Monangai
fade_watch.why: D'Andre Swift is the more efficient back, Chicago drew the league's toughest schedule, and Monangai needs positive game script he won't reliably get — a round-8 price for a contingent role.

fade_watch.name: J.J. McCarthy
fade_watch.why: Lost the Vikings job to Kyler Murray outright after posting the worst passer rating among qualified QBs in 2025 — zero standalone value until an injury, even in superflex builds.

uncertainty_note: The genuinely unsettled stuff right now: the Browns (Watson vs. Sanders) and Jets (Geno vs. Klubnik) QB jobs are live and could flip on one preseason game; Week 1 availability for the ACL returnees — Mahomes' workload ramp, Malik Nabers, Tucker Kraft, and Michael Penix Jr. — is trending positive but not confirmed; Jeremiyah Love's high-ankle timeline (3-5 weeks) could stretch into September; and every preseason snap-count read here (Titans, Packers, Raiders, Jaguars backfields and WR rooms) comes from ONE depth chart and ONE exhibition game, so treat those splits as leading indicators, not settled roles, until cut-down week.
